title: Garlic Irrigation Kenya: Drip Layout & Equipment | DripTech
description: Plan garlic irrigation in Kenya with guidance on bed layout, dripline spacing, filtration, valves and budgeting a complete system.
intro: Garlic is commonly grown in rows or raised beds, so irrigation planning should start with the bed dimensions, planting pattern, soil and water source. This guide focuses on the equipment and design decisions to check before buying a kit; it is not a fixed watering schedule for every farm.

sections.heading: Choose a system around the bed layout
paragraphs: Drip tape or inline dripline can suit dense garlic beds when emitter spacing and flow match the planting pattern and soil. Some farms also consider rain hose or sprinklers, but the choice should account for water availability, wind, disease considerations and the uniformity required across the plot.
Do not decide the number of lines per bed from acreage alone. Bed width, number of planted rows, crop spacing, soil infiltration and the dripline's wetting pattern all affect the layout.

sections.heading: Planning figures at a glance
paragraphs: These are common planning ranges, not a prescription. Variety, soil, climate, water quality and your agronomist's advice decide the final figures, so confirm them before ordering equipment.

bullets: Drip tape or inline dripline matched to bed and plant spacing

sections.heading: Estimate the complete cost—not just the dripline
paragraphs: A realistic quote should list the dripline quantity, pipe sizes, filters, fittings, valves, water supply or pump requirements, installation and any field-specific civil work. Compare quotations using the same bed layout, pressure rating, included parts and delivery assumptions.
Before ordering, record the field dimensions, bed spacing, water source, elevation changes and available flow. DripTech can use those details to help prepare a farm-specific equipment list.

faqs.q: What type of drip line suits garlic beds?
faqs.a: Drip tape or inline dripline with closely spaced emitters often suits dense garlic beds. The right choice depends on the bed width, soil and the pressure your water supply can give, so check these before choosing.

faqs.q: How many drip lines does a garlic bed need?
faqs.a: Many raised beds use one or two lines, but there is no fixed number. Bed width, number of planted rows and how far water spreads sideways in your soil decide it.

faqs.q: Do I need a filter for garlic drip irrigation?
faqs.a: Yes. Drip emitters block easily, so every drip system needs a filter matched to the water source and the emitter specification. Borehole and river water need different filtration.

faqs.q: Can DripTech prepare a quotation for my garlic farm?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the field dimensions, bed spacing, water source and available flow through the contact page, and DripTech can prepare an equipment list for your layout.

title: Passion Fruit Irrigation Kenya: Drippers & Layout | DripTech
description: Plan passion fruit irrigation in Kenya with guidance on button drippers, flow, pressure, filtration and orchard layout.
intro: Passion fruit is a trellised perennial crop, so the irrigation layout differs from closely spaced vegetable beds. The right equipment depends on vine spacing, soil, water quality, terrain and the water supply available at the farm.

sections.heading: Why orchard-style irrigation may fit
paragraphs: Button drippers connected to a lateral line are commonly considered for passion fruit because each vine is a distinct planting point. Dripper flow and the number of emitters per plant should be selected from crop stage, soil wetting, available pressure and the design—not chosen only because a particular emitter is popular.

Some farms may use other irrigation methods during establishment or for specific field conditions. Compare water distribution, pumping needs, wind exposure and the crop's disease-management requirements before deciding.

sections.heading: Planning figures at a glance
paragraphs: These are common planning ranges, not a prescription. Variety, soil, climate, water quality and your agronomist's advice decide the final figures, so confirm them before ordering equipment.

sections.heading: Information to collect before requesting a quote
paragraphs: Share the planted area, row and vine spacing, water source, approximate elevation difference, source flow and whether the crop is newly established or mature. These details help determine the number of emitters, zone sizes, pipe dimensions and pump requirements.

Avoid using a universal irrigation duration as a rule: soil texture, weather, crop stage, emitter discharge and root-zone conditions change how much water a farm needs. Confirm scheduling locally and monitor soil moisture.

faqs.q: Is drip irrigation suitable for passion fruit?
faqs.a: Drip is widely used for trellised perennial crops because water goes to the root zone along each row. The layout should follow your trellis rows and vine spacing.

faqs.q: How many emitters does each passion fruit plant need?
faqs.a: It depends on soil, climate and plant age. Many growers use one or two emitters per plant, but check the flow rate against your water supply and your agronomist's advice.

faqs.q: Should I use one lateral per row or two?
faqs.a: One lateral per row is common. Sandier soils or wider spacing can need more coverage, so check how far water spreads in your own soil.

faqs.q: What should I send to get a passion fruit quotation?
faqs.a: Send the plot dimensions, trellis row spacing, plant spacing, water source, elevation changes and available flow, and DripTech can prepare a farm-specific equipment list.

title: Macadamia Irrigation Kenya: Drippers & Design | DripTech
description: Plan a macadamia orchard irrigation system in Kenya, including tree spacing, emitters, filtration, pressure and future tree growth.
intro: Macadamia is an orchard crop, and irrigation design should account for tree spacing, root-zone development, slope, soil and the farm's water supply. A system that suits young trees may need adjustment as the canopy and root system develop.

sections.heading: Design for the orchard, not just the acreage
paragraphs: Button drippers or other suitable localized emitters may be used for widely spaced trees. The emitter count, discharge and position should be based on tree age, soil wetting pattern, water quality and available pressure. Do not assume one emitter arrangement fits every orchard.

Consider how the wetted area will change as trees mature and whether the design should allow additional emitters or separate irrigation zones in future. Uneven terrain may require pressure management to keep delivery consistent.

sections.heading: Planning figures at a glance
paragraphs: These are common planning ranges, not a prescription. Variety, soil, climate, water quality and your agronomist's advice decide the final figures, so confirm them before ordering equipment.

sections.heading: Plan for operation and maintenance
paragraphs: Check filters, valves, leaks and emitter discharge routinely. If some trees receive less water than others, compare pressure and flow at different points before changing emitter sizes or watering duration.

A useful quotation should show the block layout, pipe sizes, emitter quantities, filtration, controls, pump assumptions and expansion allowances. DripTech can help prepare a preliminary equipment list from your orchard details.

faqs.q: Do young macadamia trees need different irrigation from mature trees?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Young trees have a small root zone, so fewer emitters close to the trunk are common, and more are added as the canopy and roots grow. Plan the layout so you can extend it.

faqs.q: Is drip or sprinkler irrigation better for macadamia?
faqs.a: Both are used. Drip suits many orchards because it targets the root zone, but your slope, soil, wind and water supply should decide it.

faqs.q: How should I zone a macadamia orchard?
faqs.a: Separate valves by block help you irrigate young and mature trees, or different slopes, on their own schedules. Match zone size to the flow your pump or tank can supply.

faqs.q: What information does DripTech need to quote an orchard system?
faqs.a: Send the orchard size, tree spacing, tree age, slope or elevation change, water source and available flow so the equipment list can be sized properly.

title: Strawberry Irrigation Kenya: Dripline & Layout | DripTech
description: Plan strawberry irrigation in Kenya with guidance on bed layout, emitter spacing, filtration, fertigation compatibility and system budgeting.
intro: Strawberries are often grown in beds, containers or protected structures. The irrigation layout needs to fit the growing method, bed width, substrate or soil, and the way water and nutrients are managed.

sections.heading: Match the delivery method to the growing setup
paragraphs: Drip tape or inline dripline can suit bed production when emitter spacing and flow are matched to plant spacing and the root-zone wetting pattern. Container or substrate production may need a different emitter arrangement. Do not select line spacing based on crop name alone.
Where fruit quality and disease pressure matter, compare localized watering with overhead methods in the context of the growing environment and crop-management plan.

sections.heading: Planning figures at a glance
paragraphs: These are common planning ranges, not a prescription. Variety, soil, climate, water quality and your agronomist's advice decide the final figures, so confirm them before ordering equipment.

Share the growing method, bed dimensions, number of plants, water source and site elevation to get a more relevant preliminary equipment list. Confirm crop-specific irrigation scheduling with a qualified local agronomist and monitor moisture in the root zone.

faqs.q: Is drip irrigation good for strawberries?
faqs.a: Drip is widely used for strawberries because it applies water at the plant row and keeps foliage drier. The layout should match your bed width, plant rows and growing method.

faqs.q: How many drip lines does a strawberry bed need?
faqs.a: Many beds use one or two lines, depending on bed width and plant rows. Check how far water spreads sideways in your soil or substrate.

faqs.q: Can I fertigate strawberries through the drip system?
faqs.a: Many growers do, but it needs a compatible injector, clean water and fine filtration. Plan the fertigation equipment together with the irrigation design, not after it.

faqs.q: Does the system change for greenhouse or tunnel strawberries?
faqs.a: The principles are the same, but protected growing often needs tighter control of volumes and timing. Share your structure size and bed layout when asking for a quotation.

title: French Beans Irrigation Kenya: Dripline Layout | DripTech
description: Plan irrigation for French beans in Kenya with guidance on row layout, dripline spacing, filtration, irrigation zones and cost planning.
intro: French beans are a row crop, and irrigation design should reflect the bed or row arrangement, soil, water supply and the field's harvesting workflow. This guide helps organise the system questions before purchasing equipment.

sections.heading: Plan rows and irrigation zones first
paragraphs: Drip tape or inline dripline may be appropriate for row-grown French beans when emitter spacing and discharge suit the planting pattern and soil. The number of lines per bed depends on bed width, rows per bed, plant spacing and the wetted width; it should not be chosen from acreage alone.

Divide the field into practical zones based on flow available, pipe lengths, terrain and operational needs. A layout with too much demand in one zone may not irrigate uniformly if the source or pump cannot supply the required flow and pressure.

sections.heading: Planning figures at a glance
paragraphs: These are common planning ranges, not a prescription. Variety, soil, climate, water quality and your agronomist's advice decide the final figures, so confirm them before ordering equipment.

sections.heading: Before comparing quotations
paragraphs: Compare the same field dimensions, bed arrangement, number of lines, line specification, filtration, fittings and installation scope. Ask suppliers to state roll lengths and whether prices include transport, tax and commissioning.

Collect the source flow, elevation changes, water quality, field dimensions and crop-row layout before requesting a quote. Irrigation timing should be adjusted to weather, soil moisture and crop stage rather than copied from a generic schedule.

faqs.q: Is drip irrigation suitable for French beans?
faqs.a: Yes, drip is commonly used for row-grown French beans because water is delivered along the bed. The layout should follow your rows and picking workflow.

faqs.q: How many drip tapes do I need per French bean bed?
faqs.a: One tape per bed is common for a two-row bed, but wider beds or lighter soils can need two. Check the wetting pattern in your own soil.

faqs.q: Why should I zone French bean fields?
faqs.a: Staggered plantings are at different stages and need water at different times. Separate valves let you irrigate each block on its own schedule.

faqs.q: How do I compare French bean irrigation quotations?
faqs.a: Ask each supplier to quote the same bed layout, pressure rating, filter, valves, fittings and delivery, so the prices are comparable.
